# Third-party names and terms

## Threat-intel providers (`asa intel`)

`asa intel` enriches a finished run with answers shaped like three public threat-intel services:

| Provider | Shape mirrored by the field mapper |
|---|---|
| VirusTotal | `data.attributes.last_analysis_stats` (file, address, domain and URL reports) |
| AbuseIPDB | `data.abuseConfidenceScore`, `data.totalReports` (address checks) |
| AlienVault OTX | `pulse_info.count` (indicator "general" section) |

**The fixtures are synthetic.** `data/intel/fixtures/*.json` are generated by `tools/make_intel_fixtures.py` from a fixed seed
for documentation addresses (RFC 5737) and reserved test names. They are not real provider answers and say nothing about any real
address, domain or file. The product names are used only to describe the response shapes; no provider endorses or is affiliated
with this project.

**Real lookups are out of scope.** This package contains no network code, no API-key handling and no environment-variable
reads (a test enforces it). Anyone who adds real lookups must follow each provider's terms first; for example, the VirusTotal
public API terms are non-commercial.

## Runtime and development dependencies

The runtime needs only the Python standard library plus the `anthropic` SDK (live mode only). Exact versions and hashes are in
`requirements.lock` and `requirements-dev.lock`; the development tool is pytest.
